    Aquatics Centers

    The City of Irvine operates year-round municipal programs in unique aquatic facilities. The William Woollett Jr. Aquatics Center is a world-class venue for local, regional and national competition, with two 50-meter pools and a 25-yard instruction pool. The Northwood Aquatics Center has a 50-meter pool. Programs combine instruction, education, recreation and competition, offered by the city and local nonprofit aquatic groups.

    The city's Learn to Swim program is one of the largest municipal swimming programs in Southern California.

    4 pools
    Two 50-meter pools and a teaching pool at Woollett, a 50-meter pool at Northwood
    6am

    The centers

    Woollett Aquatics Center

    4601 Walnut Ave, Irvine, CA 92604

    • Competition Pool: 50 m, 8 lanes long course or 17 short course
    • Diving Pool: 50 m, 1- and 3-meter boards, 17 lanes short course
    • Teaching Pool: 25 yards, lessons and shallow-water lap swim

    Woollett, lane by lane

    Northwood Aquatics Center

    4515 Portola Pkwy, Irvine, CA 92620

    • 50-meter pool: 8 lanes long course or 19 short course, one-meter board
    • School use by day; clubs and city programs evenings and weekends

    Northwood, lane by lane

    Safe swims
    start here

    Join the Floatie Exchange

    Bring a non-Coast-Guard-approved floatie to the Woollett Aquatics Center during business hours and leave with a free Coast Guard-approved life jacket for a child 6 or younger. A parent or guardian watches a short safety video and signs a waiver. More on the city's page, or call 949-724-6717.
